JSON: Name: rfh_site_dependent_rcflp Title: Relax-and-fix heuristic for the capacitated reliable fixed-charge facility location problem with site-dependent failure probabilities Short Hypothesis: A relax-and-fix heuristic that fixes facility location variables, relaxes higher-level assignment variables (parameterized by α), and re-optimizes remaining binary decisions will produce statistically significantly better upper bounds within a fixed CPU time than directly solving the linearized mixed-integer formulation with a state-of-the-art MIP solver on capacitated reliable fixed-charge facility location instances with site-dependent facility failure probabilities. Related Work: Existing literature on reliable facility location extends classical p-median and fixed-charge models to account for facility failures using five main modelling paradigms: implicit-probability (IF), scenario-based (SB), reliable-backup (RB), continuum-approximation (CA), and robust optimisation (RO). Solution methods include exact and decomposition approaches (Lagrangian relaxation, Benders/column-and-constraint schemes), metaheuristics (genetic, scatter search), hybrid population-based methods, swarm-intelligence SAA, and local-search combined with cutting planes. Prior capacitated reliable models typically assume homogeneous failure probabilities or treat reliability via scenario sampling; methods that handle capacities often rely on heavy two-stage stochastic or decomposition schemes that do not scale well. Relax-and-fix (or fix-and-relax) heuristics have been effective in other MILP contexts (lot-sizing, scheduling) but have not been applied to capacitated reliable fixed-charge models with site-dependent failure probabilities. Limitations in prior work include reliance on identical failure probabilities, limited treatment of capacity exceedance under disruptions, large-scale intractability for exact solvers, and lack of tailored MIP-based heuristics that exploit level-r assignment structure. Abstract: We address the capacitated reliable fixed-charge facility location problem where facility failure probabilities are site-dependent and facilities can temporarily exceed capacity by a bounded amount after disruptions. We present a linearized mixed-integer formulation that models level-r assignments and expected disruption costs, and we propose a two-phase relax-and-fix heuristic (RFH). In the heuristic's beginning phase, facility location binaries remain integer while a configurable prefix of assignment levels is enforced as integer and the remainder relaxed; capacity-exceed indicator variables are relaxed. In the ending phase, selected variables are frozen and the remaining binaries are restored and re-optimized. We evaluate two RFH strategies and analyze parameters (assignment depth α, timelimit, MIP tolerance). The main contributions are: (1) the first linearized RCFLP model with site-dependent failure probabilities, (2) an RFH adapted to level-r assignment and capacity-exceed variables, and (3) an experimental pipeline showing RFH yields improved upper bounds and reduced runtime versus direct MIP solving on benchmark instances while enabling sensitivity analysis on capacity upgrades and failure-probability assumptions. Experiments: Datasets: - Base instances: modified OR-Library capacitated p-median instances (sizes: I={49,50,88,150} customers; J=I+1 candidate sites). For each base instance create 10 random seeds of site-dependent failure probabilities q_j sampled i.i.d. U(0,0.1). For sensitivity studies also generate two uniform-probability variants per instance: q_low = min(q_j) and q_high = max(q_j). - Capacity upgrade parameters: a ∈ {0.00,0.05,0.10,0.15} (v_j = a * c_j), b ∈ {0,3,5,7,10} (max number of facilities allowed expected capacity exceedances). Baselines: - Direct MIP: linearized formulation (LRCFLP) solved with IBM ILOG CPLEX 22.1 using default MIP settings. - RFH variants: Strategy 1 and Strategy 2 as described (begin/end phases), and RFH-MIP hybrid (use RFH solution as CPLEX warm start). - Additional baseline (where available): Lagrangian-relaxation implementation of reliable FLP (representative exact/decomposition method). Evaluation metrics: - Upper bound (UB) objective value, best UB found within timelimit. - Lower bound (LB) and MIP optimality gap = (UB-LB)/max(1,|UB|). - CPU time to best UB and total runtime. - Cost breakdown: transportation, penalty, fixed location costs. - Solution attributes: number of opened facilities, number of facilities with expected capacity exceedances, feasibility (capacity constraint violations under no-failure and expected scenarios). - Statistical comparison: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test of UB and gap across instance seeds; report median, mean, std. Experimental setup: - Hardware: single machine with 8 CPU cores and 16 GB RAM (report exact CPU and memory); software: Java implementation for RFH, CPLEX 22.1 for MIP solves. - Timelimits: primary experiments with total timelimit T_total ∈ {800s,1600s}. RFH phase split as in paper (Phase1/Phase2 times configurable), evaluate sensitivity to split. - RFH parameter sweep: α ∈ {1,2,3,4, r_max} where r_max = number of open-able backup levels; OptGap tolerance values used by CPLEX in each phase: {1e-4,1e-3}. Ablation studies: 1) Vary α while holding timelimit constant to quantify impact of assignment-level relaxation depth on UB and runtime. 2) Compare Strategy1 vs Strategy2 vs RFH-MIP to isolate the effect of relaxing assignment variables versus fixing them to zero in Phase1. 3) Warm-start effect: run RFH for T_total/2, then run CPLEX warm-started with RFH solution for T_total/2; compare to single-run CPLEX T_total. 4) Failure-probability model ablation: solve with site-dependent q_j, uniform q_low, and uniform q_high and compare resulting UBs and opened-facility decisions. Repetitions: for each instance-seed-parameter combination run 1 deterministic solve (randomness arises only in instance generation); aggregate metrics over seeds and report 95% confidence intervals. Risk Factors and Limitations: Model and data assumptions: - Independent failure assumption: the model assumes independent facility failures; correlated failures (regional disasters) are not modelled and may invalidate expected-cost calculations. - Known site-dependent probabilities: q_j are assumed known and accurate; misestimation will bias decisions and invalidate experimental conclusions. Technical and algorithmic risks: - Linearization blow-up: introducing W_{ijr} variables for P*Y products increases problem size substantially; memory exhaustion or long solve times for MIP and RFH subproblems is possible for large J and r. - Heuristic local optimality: RFH may converge to suboptimal local solutions dependent on α and variable ordering; results may be sensitive to parameter choices and seed instances. - Solver-dependent behavior: RFH performance relies on CPLEX behaviour on relaxed subproblems; different solvers or versions may yield different empirical results. Scalability and compute limits: - Instances beyond tested sizes (>>150 nodes) may be intractable due to RAM and time limits; lower bounds may be weak or unavailable for very large instances, preventing reliable gap estimates. Evaluation biases and generalization limits: - Benchmark bias: OR-Library instances are synthetic with Euclidean distances; real-world network topologies, multi-product flows, or correlated demand/failure patterns may produce different outcomes. - Emergency-facility modelling and penalty cost φ: single-parameter emergency modelling could distort assignment patterns compared with richer service-level models. - Capacity exceedance modelling: modelling expected exceedance via V and U variables abstracts dynamic redistribution and may not capture temporal/operational constraints during disruptions.
